data.narrative:
Parallel Systems is a Series A-stage transportation company founded by Matt Soule, John Howard, and Ben Stabler that has raised $100M to date. The relevant comp universe consists of 8 private frontier-tech transportation firms, including Rivian, The Boring Company, Einride, Pipedream, and FleetZero. No public transportation comparables exist at an analogous stage and valuation tier.

The valuation analysis relies on a single applicable method: stage-progression analysis. Using total capital raised ($100M) as a proxy baseline, the method applies a 2.0x multiplier typical of Series A-to-subsequent-stage step-ups, yielding an implied valuation of $12M. A peer-median approach was not applicable due to insufficient same-stage and adjacent-stage comparables within the narrow transportation sector cohort—while three transportation peers exist, none met the three-datapoint threshold required for statistical reliability.

The triangulated analysis supports a valuation range of $10M to $14M, with a central estimate of $12M. This range reflects limited triangulation coverage, as reliance on a single method introduces material uncertainty around the point estimate. Key uncertainties include the appropriateness of the 2.0x step-up multiplier for this specific company's risk and growth profile, as well as the representativeness of the broader private transportation comp set for early-stage frontier-tech positioning. A second valuation method would materially strengthen conviction in this range.
